prompt: Many countries invest heavily in training doctors, engineers and other skilled professionals, only for large numbers of them to emigrate soon after qualifying. Why does this happen, and what measures could reduce it?
essay:
In many developing countries, the government is spending a lot of money for the education of the doctors and engineers, but after the graduation these people are leaving the country and going to work abroad. This phenomenon is called brain drain and it is a big problem for these countries.

There are some reasons for this problem. Firstly, the salary in the foreign countries is much higher. A doctor can earn maybe five times more in a developed country, so it is normal that he wants to go there. Secondly, the working condition in the home country is not good. In many hospitals there is not enough equipment and the doctors are working very long hours. Moreover, some people are going abroad because they want a better future for their children, for example a better education and a better life quality.

This problem can be solved in different ways. Firstly, the government should increase the salary of these professionals so they will not leave. Secondly, the government can make a rule that the students who studied with the government money must work in the country for some years, otherwise they have to pay back the money. In addition, the government should invest more in the hospitals and the universities to make the working condition better.

In conclusion, the main reasons of the brain drain are the low salary, the bad working condition and the search of a better life, and the government should increase the salary, make a compulsory service and improve the facilities. Only in this way the country can keep its talented people.
title: When trained graduates leave the country that educated them
